results.input: Aria Voss is trapped in the Ice Citadel. Suggest an escape that uses fire magic.
results.answer:
Aria can cast fire magic in the Citadel. The ban is that fire magic fails inside the Citadel unless the caster possesses flint, and she carries flint, so she meets the exception [d40003b6]. Her state shows 20 mana, and a fire bolt costs 12 [eac3e3c8]. That gives her one bolt, not two.

The lore disagrees on whether she must strike the flint. The Visitor's Primer says to strike it on steel before every casting [8f22b8dd]. The Glass Library's law says carrying it is enough [d40003b6]. Nobody has tested which is right [8f22b8dd]. The lore doesn't say whether her broken sword counts as steel.

Options:
1. Use the one bolt on a lock, bar or door. This is your story's choice, since the lore doesn't describe the Citadel's doors.
2. Wait for the Night of Thaw. The eastern wall is unwarded then, but that only helps teleportation, and the Eastern Postern guard is doubled [c8557954].
3. Use ordinary fire from a torch or candle. It burns normally because it isn't a spell [d40003b6].
evidence: [fetch_character_state] Aria Voss is at Ice Citadel, condition healthy, mana 20, health 85, carries: flint, broken sword, health potion

[search_lore] passage d40003b6 (The Magic of Aethel > Casting Rules > Fire magic and the Ice Citadel): Fire magic cannot be cast inside the Ice Citadel unless the caster possesses flint. The walls of the Citadel are woven with the Frost Binding, an old working that smothers every spell of the Fire discipline the moment it is cast. Flint is the single exception, because a flint holds a stolen spark that the Frost Binding recognises and lets pass.

Possession means carrying the flint on one's person. It does not have to be struck, held in the hand or shown to anyone. A caster with a flint in a pocket can cast fire magic anywhere inside the Citadel.

The ban applies to magic only. Torches, candles, forge fires and the Great Hearth burn normally inside the Citadel, because ordinary fire is not a spell.
[search_lore] passage d217db3d (Ember Keep > Rules of the Keep > Frost magic in Ember Keep): Frost magic costs double mana inside Ember Keep. The heat of the volcano pushes against every working of the Frost discipline, so a frost lance that costs 15 mana anywhere else costs 30 mana inside the Keep. Fire magic is not affected, and it costs the normal price.
[search_lore] passage c8557954 (The Ice Citadel > The Wards > The Night of Thaw): Once a year, on the last night of the Long Winter, the eastern wall of the Citadel is unwarded. The ward on the eastern wall goes down at midnight and comes back up at dawn. The Wardens say that the ice must be allowed to breathe while the Frost Binding renews itself.

During the Night of Thaw the eastern wall can be crossed by teleportation like any open ground, and the guard on the Eastern Postern is doubled. The other three walls stay warded. The Frost Binding that smothers fire magic stays in force all night, so fire magic is still impossible inside the Citadel on the Night of Thaw unless the caster possesses flint.
[search_lore] passage eac3e3c8 (The Magic of Aethel > The Three Disciplines): There are three disciplines of magic. Fire, also called pyromancy, creates and shapes flame and heat. Frost, also called cryomancy, creates and shapes ice and cold. Aether covers everything that works on distance and boundaries: teleportation, wards and scrying.

A minor spell of any discipline costs between 5 and 15 mana. A fire bolt costs 12 mana and a frost lance costs 15 mana. Greater workings, such as summoning a storm, cost far more and are limited to Archmages.
[search_lore] passage 8f22b8dd (The Ice Citadel > The Visitor's Primer): The Wardens give every visitor a short booklet called the Visitor's Primer. It lists the rules of the Citadel in plain words. It says that a visitor who wishes to cast fire magic must strike their flint on the steel before every casting, and that an unstruck flint is not enough.

This instruction does not agree with the law of magic recorded in the Archive of the Glass Library, which says that carrying the flint is enough. Visitors who have followed the Primer and struck their flint have never been refused, so nobody has tested which rule is right.
[search_lore] passage 275bf749 (History and Factions of Aethel > The Founding of the Ice Citadel): In Year 31 the Warden-General Isolde Frane led a band of survivors north to the Northern Reach and began to build the Ice Citadel. She chose the site because the ice there was the oldest in the world and the cold slowed the wild mana that the Sundering had released. The Frost Binding, the working that smothers fire magic inside the walls, was her first great spell. She had learned it from a flint-bearer, a person who carried a flint as a token of an older craft, and she made flint the single exception to the Binding in thanks.

results.input: Aria Voss needs to leave the Ice Citadel at once. Have her teleport out and describe how.
results.answer:
Aria can't teleport out as things stand, for two reasons.

1. The ban: all four walls are warded, and teleportation can't cross a warded wall in either direction [1fe24429][57e9dcc6]. The exception is the eastern wall on the Night of Thaw, the last night of the Long Winter, from midnight to dawn [c8557954]. I can't tell from the lore whether it is that night in your story.
2. The cost: teleportation costs 50 mana [57e9dcc6], and Aria has 20. She doesn't meet that either.

Options:
1. Change the story: set the scene on the Night of Thaw and restore her to at least 50 mana. She can then teleport through the eastern wall, though the Eastern Postern guard is doubled [c8557954].
2. Change the story: have the Warden-General lower a ward with the seal for one hour [f34602a1]. Aria would still need 50 mana.
3. Have her leave on foot by the Gate of Frost, the main entrance [1fe24429]. The lore doesn't say how it is guarded, so that part is yours to decide.

[search_lore] passage 010e67cb (Ember Keep > Rules of the Keep > The Keep has no wards): Ember Keep has never been warded. The Ember Court holds that walls are for those who are afraid of their neighbours, and has refused every offer of a ward. A caster can therefore teleport into the Keep, or out of it, for the normal price of 50 mana.
[search_lore] passage c8557954 (The Ice Citadel > The Wards > The Night of Thaw): Once a year, on the last night of the Long Winter, the eastern wall of the Citadel is unwarded. The ward on the eastern wall goes down at midnight and comes back up at dawn. The Wardens say that the ice must be allowed to breathe while the Frost Binding renews itself.

During the Night of Thaw the eastern wall can be crossed by teleportation like any open ground, and the guard on the Eastern Postern is doubled. The other three walls stay warded. The Frost Binding that smothers fire magic stays in force all night, so fire magic is still impossible inside the Citadel on the Night of Thaw unless the caster possesses flint.
[search_lore] passage f34602a1 (The Ice Citadel > The Wards > How the wards work): The four walls of the Citadel are protected by wards that were raised after the founding of the fortress. They stop teleportation and scrying. Only the Warden-General can lower a ward, with the seal of the Frost Wardens, and only for one hour at a time.
[search_lore] passage efeb2d52 (The Magic of Aethel > Casting Rules > Wards): A ward is a working of the Aether discipline that is anchored to a wall or a threshold. A warded wall blocks teleportation and scrying in both directions. A ward stays in place until it is broken or until it expires, and most wards are renewed every year by the Aether-mages who keep them.

Only a seal of the Frost Wardens can lower a ward, and only for one hour at a time. The Warden-General alone holds the seal of the Ice Citadel.
[search_lore] passage 57e9dcc6 (The Magic of Aethel > Casting Rules > Teleportation): Teleportation costs 50 mana and cannot cross warded walls. The caster names a destination within one league (about five kilometres) and arrives there at once. A caster can carry only what they can carry on their own body. A teleporting caster cannot take another person with them.

Teleportation fails if the straight line to the destination crosses a warded wall, in either direction. A caster can teleport out of a warded place only if the path out does not cross a ward, which in practice almost never happens.
[search_lore] passage 1fe24429 (The Ice Citadel > Layout > The four walls): The Citadel has four walls: north, south, east and west. All four are warded. A warded wall cannot be crossed by teleportation, in either direction, so nobody can teleport into the Citadel or out of it. The western wall holds the Gate of Frost, which is the main entrance. The eastern wall holds a small door called the Eastern Postern, which is kept barred and guarded all year.

results.input: Sera Quill wants to open the Restricted Stacks of the Glass Library to read the blood-casting treatises. How can she get in?
results.answer:
Sera is in the Glass Library and carries a silver key, which is what the Restricted Stacks door requires [d5a7cf5b]. The ban is that only a silver key opens it. The only keys are the three that exist: the Head Archivist's, the Deputy Archivist's and the Keeper of the Concord's [d5a7cf5b]. Whether her key is one of those three, or a copy, isn't in your lore, so that is your call.

Options:
1. If her key is one of the three, she simply unlocks the door. This needs no magic, which matters because all spellcasting is silenced inside the Library unless the caster is a sworn Archivist [43a85e83].
2. If her key is not one of the three, she can't open the door as the lore stands. Making it one of them, for example by having it lent by a keyholder, would be a story change.
3. To keep what she reads, she must copy it by hand with the Library's own ink [a4d79694]. The lore doesn't say whether her ink vial is Library ink, and no book may leave the Library [a4d79694].
evidence: [fetch_character_state] Sera Quill is at Glass Library, condition wounded, mana 75, health 60, carries: spellbook, silver key, ink vial

[search_lore] passage d5a7cf5b (The Glass Library > Rules of the Library > The Restricted Stacks): The Restricted Stacks are a sealed wing of the Library where the most dangerous texts are kept, including the treatises on blood-casting. The door of the Restricted Stacks can be opened only with a silver key. There are exactly three silver keys. The Head Archivist holds one, the Deputy Archivist holds the second, and the Keeper of the Concord holds the third.
[search_lore] passage 3f724e69 (History and Factions of Aethel > The Concord of Glass): The Concord of Glass was signed in the Glass Library in Year 219 by the Warden-General, the Ember Regent and the Head Archivist. It has four terms. First, blood-casting is forbidden, and the Archivists have the right to inspect any caster suspected of it. Second, the Glass Library is neutral ground, and no weapon may be drawn inside it. Third, the wards of the Ice Citadel are recognised as the Wardens' own affair. Fourth, Ember Keep may stay unwarded, as the Ember Court wishes, and no ward may be raised around it without the Court's consent.
[search_lore] passage 43a85e83 (The Glass Library > Rules of the Library > Magic inside the Library): All magic is silenced inside the Glass Library, except for spells cast by a sworn Archivist. The glass walls absorb every working of every discipline, so a visitor who tries to cast a spell inside the Library simply feels the mana drain away with no effect. A spellbook can be read inside the Library, but nothing can be cast from it.
[search_lore] passage 2c6190be (The Glass Library > The Archive of the Concord): The Library keeps the original text of the Concord of Glass, the treaty that ended the War of Embers. The Concord is displayed in a case of clear glass in the central hall, and any visitor may read it for free. The Archivists are the guardians of the Concord and have the right to inspect any caster suspected of blood-casting.
[search_lore] passage a4d79694 (The Glass Library > Rules of the Library > Borrowing and copying): No book may leave the Library. A visitor who wishes to keep a text must copy it by hand, using the Library's own ink, which is sold at the Door of Quiet in sealed vials. Copies made with any other ink are treated as forgeries and confiscated.
[search_lore] passage d9ce8de8 (The Glass Library > Rules of the Library > The Library is warded): The Glass Library is warded on all sides. Teleportation cannot cross its walls, in either direction. Visitors arrive by the road, and the only way in is through the Door of Quiet on the southern side.

judge.reasoning: The answer says the door needs a silver key, that exactly three exist and who holds them, that magic is silenced, and that copies need Library ink. All of this is supported by the cited passages. Saying the lore doesn't cover whether her key is one of the three is honest. Faithfulness is 5. Constraint 1 passes. Constraint 2 requires reporting a conflict where the lore says she holds no key. The evidence contains no such statement: the lore only names three holders, and Sera is not among them. The answer does not report a conflict between the record and the lore. It frames the question as whether her key is one of the three, which only hints at the tension. That is a fail.

results.input: Kael Draven wants to go down to the lower galleries of the Hollow Mine. Have him light his lantern inside the mine and climb down with his rope and pickaxe.
results.answer:
Kael can't do this as written, for two reasons.

1. Lighting the lantern underground is banned. Fire magic and open flames are both forbidden in the Hollow Mine because of firedamp. A caster who breaks the ban is expelled and fined. Sealed lanterns are lit with a spark from outside the mine [8db439a2]. Kael is the one caster allowed to carry a sealed lantern into the lower galleries [90e82dff]. That exception covers carrying it, not lighting it inside. The lore doesn't say whether his lantern is sealed.

2. He has no rope or pickaxe. His record shows only a lantern and a cracked mask. The lore says nothing about where he could get them.

Options:
1. Kael steps outside, lights the lantern with a spark there, then re-enters and descends. This works if the lantern is sealed, which you would need to confirm.
2. Add a rope and pickaxe to his inventory. This is a story change.
3. Have him go down with the lantern already lit from outside, and add the gear as a change.

Open flames are forbidden too. Miners use sealed lanterns, which are lit with a spark from outside the mine. A caster who casts a fire spell inside the mine is expelled and fined.

The Guild also keeps the only map of the lower galleries.

results.input: Mira Sol is wounded. Have her heal herself and then teleport across the harbor wall of Salt Harbour.
results.answer:
Two parts, and the lore only settles one.

Healing: the lore I found has no rule for self-healing or its mana cost, so I can't say whether she can do it or what it takes. She has 100 mana, and teleporting costs 80 [28b93d4d]. That leaves 20 for healing, and I don't know if that's enough.

Teleporting: the Tide Wards on the harbour walls block teleportation in both directions [4add25e6]. Teleporting across a warded wall needs a Tide-key [28b93d4d]. Mira carries only a star chart, and she owes the Council for a lost key [afb9b066]. So she can't do it as things stand.

The exception is the full-moon hour. The wards are lowered for one hour, and a caster can cross for the normal 80 mana without a key [4add25e6]. Your notes don't say whether it is full moon now.

Options:
1. Set the scene within the full-moon hour (a timing change).
2. Give her a Tide-key (a new item, issued only by the Harbour Council [eb279661]).
3. Have her cross without teleporting (a change to the plan).
evidence: [fetch_character_state] Mira Sol is at Salt Harbour, condition wounded, mana 100, health 45, carries: star chart

[search_lore] passage 4add25e6 (Places of Nox > Salt Harbour > The Tide Wards): The harbour walls are warded. The wards are called the Tide Wards, and they block teleportation in either direction. They are lowered for one hour at every full moon so that ships' crews can teleport their cargo ashore. During that hour a caster can teleport across the harbour walls for the normal price of 80 mana, without a Tide-key.
[search_lore] passage 28b93d4d (The Magic of Nox > Casting Rules > Teleportation): Teleportation costs 80 mana in Nox. It can cross a warded wall only if the caster carries a Tide-key, a small disc of grey shell that is issued by the Harbour Council. Without a Tide-key, teleportation cannot cross a warded wall.
[search_lore] passage eb279661 (Places of Nox > Salt Harbour): Salt Harbour is the great port of Nox, a city of white stone and tall masts on a bay of green water. About twelve thousand people live there. It is ruled by the Harbour Council, a body of nine ship-captains, and it is the only place in Nox where Tide-keys are issued.
[search_lore] passage 15f296c1 (Places of Nox > Salt Harbour > The Council House): The Council House stands on the quay. It is the only building in Nox that keeps a register of every Tide-key. A lost Tide-key must be reported within a day, and a replacement costs a month's wages.
[search_lore] passage afb9b066 (Notable Characters of Nox > Mira Sol): Mira Sol is a navigator from Salt Harbour who learned to read the stars from her grandmother. She is a Tidemaster, with a mana pool of up to 300 mana, and one of the few in Nox who can teleport between ships at sea. She is bold, talkative and in debt.

Mira owes the Harbour Council the price of a lost Tide-key. She says that it was stolen, and the Council says that it was sold.

Open flames are forbidden too. Miners use sealed lanterns, which are lit with a spark from outside the mine. A caster who casts a fire spell inside the mine is expelled and fined.

It honestly says no healing rule was found. Faithfulness is 5. Constraint 1 fails because the answer does not say healing costs 80 mana. 2. The Visitor's Primer says a visitor must strike flint on steel before every casting, and that an unstruck flint is not enough [8f22b8dd]. The notes say nobody has tested which rule is right [8f22b8dd].

Aria has no steel in her inventory, so she cannot follow the Primer's rule as written. Her options:

2. Get a piece of steel and strike the flint first, as the Primer says. This is a story change, because she doesn't carry steel now.
3. Settle the conflict yourself, for example by deciding which source is right.

results.input: Sera Quill is wounded. Have her heal herself so she can keep working.
results.answer:
Sera can't heal herself, for two reasons.

1. Healing is barred for the healer's own body: "a healer cannot heal themselves" [d0ce63f5]. The passage gives no exception.
2. She is in the Glass Library, where all magic is silenced except spells cast by a sworn Archivist [43a85e83]. Her mana would just drain away. Her notes don't say she is a sworn Archivist, so she doesn't meet the exception as far as I can see. Even if she were, reason 1 still applies.

Options:
1. She leaves the Library and another healer treats her. Each wound costs that healer 25 mana [d0ce63f5].
2. A sworn Archivist who can heal treats her inside the Library [43a85e83]. That would be a new character, so it is a story change.
3. She keeps working while wounded and gets healed later. This needs no change.

results.input: How many dragons live in the Cinderlands?
results.answer: Your lore doesn't say how many dragons live in the Cinderlands, and none of the passages I found mention dragons at all. The closest hits are about the Ember Court, which rules the Cinderlands [f21f0e20], and its army, the Cinder Guard, which numbers about nine hundred soldiers [a5dfa6d0]. If dragons exist in your world, that is a gap in the canon. I can help you brainstorm a number or a role for them, but that would be a new addition to your world.

results.input: Can Mira Sol cast fire magic while she is in Salt Harbour? Does she need flint?
results.answer:
Yes, she can. Mira is in Salt Harbour with full mana (100), though she is wounded.

The only ban on fire magic is inside the Hollow Mine, because of the firedamp [1c9fa262][8db439a2]. Salt Harbour is not the mine, so the ban doesn't apply to her. The lore passages I found mention no fire restriction for Salt Harbour itself. Its Tide Wards only block teleportation [4add25e6].

She doesn't need flint. Fire magic can be cast anywhere in Nox without any special object, and flint has no meaning for magic there [1c9fa262]. She is only carrying a star chart anyway.

[search_lore] passage 8db439a2 (Places of Nox > The Hollow Mine > Fire in the Hollow Mine): Fire magic of any kind is forbidden inside the Hollow Mine, because the air holds firedamp. Open flames are forbidden too. Miners use sealed lanterns, which are lit with a spark from outside the mine. A caster who casts a fire spell inside the mine is expelled and fined.
[search_lore] passage 4add25e6 (Places of Nox > Salt Harbour > The Tide Wards): The harbour walls are warded. The wards are called the Tide Wards, and they block teleportation in either direction. They are lowered for one hour at every full moon so that ships' crews can teleport their cargo ashore. During that hour a caster can teleport across the harbour walls for the normal price of 80 mana, without a Tide-key.

results.input: Mira Sol is on the deck of a ship under an open night sky. Can she cast a minor spell without spending any mana?
results.answer:
Yes, as far as the lore shows. A caster under an open night sky can draw on starlight to cast one minor spell without paying mana. This works once per night, and only for spells that cost 15 mana or less [1e1ff2d6]. Mira meets the sky condition, so the spell must cost 15 mana or less and she must not have used starlight yet tonight.

Her state puts her at Salt Harbour. The only place rule I found there is the Tide Wards, which block teleportation across the harbour walls [4add25e6]. The lore I found says nothing that stops starlight casting there, so a non-teleport minor spell is unaffected. A teleport would not be a minor spell anyway, since it costs 80 mana.

I can't tell whether she has already used tonight's starlight, because the story state doesn't track that.
